request_summary: Apply the agent optimizations AG-8 (usage logging), AG-3 (explicit output token budget), AG-2 (dynamic batching) and AG-9 (water-filling document allocation with truncation logging).
rationale: C1: 5 edit-target files in one package, no one-way door — pre-declared write scope required (5 edit-target files / 0 package(s) / 1 write-scope clusters / co-change unassessed / shape=scaffolded)
entry_point: AI test generation from the Assistant chat: sending a request with an attached SRS produces cases while data/logs records per-call token usage, and no batch silently exceeds the model output budget.
done_oracle: Agent optimizations are applied: each chatCompletion logs prompt/completion/cached tokens to AiLoggingService (AG-8); output token budget is explicit and separate from the context window, with max_tokens always sent (AG-3); batch size derives from the token budget instead of the hard-coded 2, and generateScript forces one screen per batch (AG-2); document allocation uses water-filling so a small file no longer starves a large one, and truncation is logged with delivered/requested counts (AG-9). Existing AI tests stay green and no existing test assertion is weakened.

seam_claims.note: max_tokens is only sent when configured > 0, so with the shipped maxTokens=0 the output budget is whatever the provider defaults to - unmeasured and unreported.

seam_claims.quote: int batchSize = 2; // 2 screens per LLM batch ensures sufficient output token capacity for 8-10 cases
seam_claims.note: Batch size is a hard-coded 2 regardless of the model budget or whether scripts are generated, so a script-bearing batch can silently overrun and lose the last case to JSON repair.
